source: House of Commons Library 2024 constituency + candidate named CSVs, read from emagar/caso-pc-oto2024 GitHub third-party copies
A: Does adding final-vote fragmentation materially improve turnout fit in geographically held-out territories vs training mean and margin-only models?

B.H0: Adding margin and ENP improves MAE ≥0.5pp

C.execution: Deterministic grouped cross-validation on the same 650 rows with full group holdout by nation (4) and region (12). Fit ordinary least squares on remaining groups: constant mean M0, realized margin M1, margin+ENP M2. Metrics MAE and RMSE across all held-out constituencies, no random split and no hyperparam tuning.

F: Fragmentation adds no material out-of-region explanatory value beyond final margin. These are SAME-ELECTION retrospective explanations using variables unavailable pre-election (realized votes), NOT forecasts or model validation of future elections.
G: Only four nations; grouped region CV shares same nationwide 2024 election and training distributions, not external issuer/year replication; original direct binary not captured.
I: No individual voter or named representative prediction
J: R5 stop 650 election panels unless original authentic source or 2019/2029 independent temporally heldout data acquired; leave Codex task.
